request.spec:
The header shows the signed-in user the due-totals of the people they watch, added up (0.00 when
watching no one).
request.prompt:
You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to
DESIGN.md for the app's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
The header shows the signed-in user the due-totals of the people they watch, added up (0.00 when
watching no one).

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit
records it expects — match them. Run `bin/e2e` to build the app, start it, and run the test as
you work; iterate until it passes. Change whatever the request needs across the app — its stored
data, its server and its front end. Do NOT edit bin/build, bin/start, bin/stop, bin/e2e,
AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
The header now shows a "Watched total" with the due-totals of the people the signed-in user watches, added up. It shows 0.00 when they watch no one. All 4 acceptance tests pass in `bin/e2e`.

**What changed:** only the front end, in `src/main/frontend/src/app/features/people/people.ts`. The app already kept track of who each user watches and sent that with each person's data, so the server and stored data didn't need to change.
- A new header entry, `watched-due-total`, sits next to "My reviews" (line 265).
- A new `watchedDueTotal` (line 1110) adds up each watched person's due-total, using the same figure shown in their row. If the sheet has a cap, each person's figure is capped first, and anyone whose due-total is n/a counts as 0. The total isn't trimmed afterwards.

**Build crash:** the first `bin/e2e` run failed because Java crashed partway through the build. It looked like a fault on this machine rather than anything in the code: a plain rerun built and passed. I deleted the crash report and core dump files it left in the project folder.
